problem_text:
A logistics firm must coordinate a circuit of maintenance checks across six regional depots, positioned at the following grid points:
Depot Alpha: (104,145)
Depot Beta: (130,79)
Depot Gamma: (166,91)
Depot Delta: (99,168)
Depot Epsilon: (64,39)
Depot Zeta: (143,176)

The travel distances between depots, in kilometers, are predetermined:
Alpha to Gamma: 82.2 km
Alpha to Delta: 23.5 km
Alpha to Epsilon: 113.3 km
Alpha to Zeta: 49.8 km
Beta to Gamma: 37.9 km
Beta to Delta: 94.2 km
Beta to Epsilon: 77.2 km
Beta to Zeta: 97.9 km
Gamma to Delta: 102.1 km
Gamma to Epsilon: 114.5 km
Gamma to Zeta: 88.1 km
Delta to Epsilon: 133.7 km
Delta to Zeta: 44.7 km
Epsilon to Zeta: 158.1 km

Direct travel between Depot Alpha and Depot Beta is not permitted due to a permanent route closure. Furthermore, the final routing plan is required to incorporate exactly one—but not both—of the following two critical connections: the link between Depot Beta and Depot Gamma, or the link between Depot Gamma and Depot Delta.

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a closed loop that visits each depot precisely one time before returning to the origin point.
